title: Ladybird browser launches alpha for macOS and Linux, first new engine in years
content:
Ladybird, an independent web browser built from scratch, has entered an alpha testing phase on macOS and Linux. On Monday, developer Andreas Kling announced the launch after more than four years of development, marking the first browser in years to ship with an entirely new engine.

The release positions Ladybird alongside the three dominant engines—Gecko, Blink, and WebKit—that power today’s most popular browsers. Gecko, now used in Mozilla Firefox, first appeared in Netscape 6 in 2000, while WebKit debuted in Apple’s Safari in 2003 as a fork of KDE’s KHTML.

A Windows version of Ladybird is also in the “later stages” of the project, indicating that support for the platform will follow the current macOS and Linux alpha releases.
summary: Ladybird, an independent web browser with a built‑from‑scratch engine, entered alpha testing on macOS and Linux, announced by developer Andreas Kling. A Windows version is planned for later stages, and the release marks the first browser in years to use an entirely new engine.
author: The Verge

title: The Verge releases 2026 holiday gift guide featuring smart rings and beat machines
content:
The Verge has released its 2026 holiday gift guide, describing gift‑giving as more than simply purchasing items within a budget. The guide emphasizes that gifts are a way to show love and demonstrate how well one knows the recipient.  

In compiling the guide, The Verge spent hours curating a selection of favorites to help readers get ahead of their holiday shopping. The list includes a range of items such as minimalist smart rings, Play‑Doh flowers, and sleek beat machines, among others. The guide promises that, regardless of a recipient’s demands, there is an exceptional option available for every special someone.
summary: The Verge compiled a 2026 holiday gift guide that includes items such as minimalist smart rings, Play‑Doh flowers and sleek beat machines. The guide is intended to help shoppers find exceptional gifts for a variety of recipients.
author: The Verge

title: GTA VI leak hacker Arion Kurtaj sentenced to seven years, released on licence
content:
Arion Kurtaj, who pleaded guilty last week to hacking Rockstar Games and other firms such as Uber and Revolut, was sentenced to seven years in prison but was released on licence, according to the BBC. The court heard that after breaching Rockstar’s systems, Kurtaj leaked 90 videos of Grand Theft Auto VI in 2022, well before the game’s public release last week.  

Before his sentencing, Kurtaj had spent time in a hospital because of his autism and also served time in prison. During the hearing, the judge described him as “a very talented young man” and urged him not to waste his talents in and out of prison.
summary: Arion Kurtaj pleaded guilty to hacking Rockstar Games and other firms and was sentenced to seven years in prison. He was released on licence after sentencing, having previously spent time in a hospital because of his autism and in prison.
author: The Verge

title: Kagi launches public beta of Kagi Mail email service
content:
Kagi, known for its paid alternative to Google Search and its Orion browser that competes with Chrome, has announced a public beta of Kagi Mail. The new email service promises “no surveillance, no ads, open standards, and no lock‑in.” Users receive an @kagimail.com address, with support for unlimited aliases and domains, 50 GB of storage, and a built‑in calendar.

Kagi’s roadmap for the service includes the addition of contacts and an address book in Q1 2027, while native mobile apps are slated for release in Q3 2027. The announcement positions Kagi Mail as a privacy‑focused competitor to Gmail.
summary: Kagi announced a public beta of Kagi Mail, an email service offering @kagimail.com addresses, unlimited aliases, 50 GB storage and a built‑in calendar. The service is described as having no surveillance, no ads, open standards and no lock‑in, with contacts slated for Q1 2027 and native mobile apps for Q3 2027.
author: The Verge

title: Asus ProArt P16 laptop adds Nvidia RTX Spark and up to 128 GB RAM, starts at $7,000
content:
A recent review notes that the Asus ProArt P16 incorporates Nvidia’s new RTX Spark chip, positioning the laptop as a potential platform for local artificial‑intelligence workloads. According to the review, the device foregoes a traditional GPU but supplies up to 128 GB of memory, which the author describes as “staggering” for running AI models directly on the machine. Nvidia markets RTX Spark as a single solution for AI, productivity and gaming, and the ProArt P16 is presented as capable of serving as a primary gaming and productivity computer despite that claim.

The reviewer cautions that the unified experience carries a high price tag, citing a top‑end configuration that costs $7,000. While Windows makes local AI more approachable, the article emphasizes that using AI on the laptop still involves considerable trial and error.
summary: The Asus ProArt P16 incorporates Nvidia’s RTX Spark chip and can be configured with up to 128 GB of memory for running local AI models. The top‑end version costs about $7,000 and, while usable for gaming and productivity, local AI still requires significant trial and error.
author: Ars Technica

title: Las Vegas Grand Prix delivers unprecedented low‑speed, slipstream‑focused race
content: Las Vegas welcomed Formula 1 to its streets this past weekend. And for the first time since the event’s inception in 2023, the Grand Prix delivered on a long-promised spectacle. The racing was closer to an IndyCar oval race than anything F1 fans will have seen since slipstreaming was the order of the day at places like Monza and Hockenheim, back when humans were still landing on the Moon and downforce had yet to fundamentally change racing. The Vegas street circuit—the one that looks like an upside-down pig—is an extreme outlier on the calendar. It has plenty of long straights, so this year’s cars still suffer from energy starvation throughout the lap, as the inadequate size of their lithium-ion hybrid batteries means they become depleted very quickly, leaving the cars on just over half power with their V6 engines operating without the benefit of the hybrid’s electric motor. But the 17 turns are mostly all low speed, so there’s no risk of seeing the cars driving demoralizingly slowly through corners that are supposed to test one’s mettle. Read full article Comments
summary: Las Vegas hosted a Formula 1 Grand Prix on its street circuit this past weekend, the first event since its 2023 debut to deliver a promised spectacle. The race’s long straights and mostly low‑speed corners caused hybrid battery depletion, leaving cars at just over half power and creating an IndyCar‑like, slipstream‑heavy style.
author: Ars Technica

title: Trump orders halt to Iowa lead‑azide detonation, cites governor‑elect Rob Sand
content:
President Trump announced on social media that he has ordered the U.S. military to stop plans to detonate 68 deteriorating barrels of lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa. He said the disposition of the unstable explosive material now rests with a federal court and with Rob Sand, Iowa’s governor‑elect, who will not assume office until January.

The Army had scheduled the detonation for November 20, but postponed it on Thursday after public outcry and a legal challenge from environmental groups. The planned explosion was expected to create a plume of toxic gases and neurotoxic lead that could travel up to 100 miles from the facility.

Iowa residents and officials reported that they learned of the detonation only days in advance. Environmental groups, led by Earthjustice, filed an emergency court petition asserting that the Army had not fully explored safer disposal options for the lead azide before planning the blast.
summary: Trump orders halt to Iowa lead‑azide detonation, cites governor‑elect Rob Sand.
author: Ars Technica

title: CrowdStrike to acquire Zscaler for $44 billion
content: CrowdStrike announced it will acquire Zscaler for $44 billion. The cybersecurity firm said the purchase of Zscaler, a provider of zero‑trust products to large enterprises, is intended to better equip its customers to use AI agents.
summary: CrowdStrike announced a deal to buy Zscaler for $44 billion. The cybersecurity giant said the acquisition will better equip their customers to use AI agents.
author: TechCrunch

title: Supertake raises $20M to let AI agents create stock portfolios from market predictions
content: Supertake, a startup, announced a $20 million financing round. The company’s platform uses AI agents to transform users’ market predictions into stock portfolios, enabling investors to allocate money to their ideas without selecting individual stocks themselves.
summary: Supertake raised $20 million. The startup lets users invest by having AI agents turn their market predictions into stock portfolios, so they don’t have to pick individual stocks themselves.
author: TechCrunch

title: Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia as CEO, greeted by staff in Silicon Valley
content: Huang receives hero’s welcome at firm’s Silicon Valley headquarters as return cements role as key AI figure Jensen Huang made his return to Nvidia’s headquarters with a hero’s welcome on Monday. Hours earlier he’d been reinstated as the CEO of the world’s most valuable chip company, following a whiplash series of events that involved a romantic affair with a suspected Chinese spy, a drastic plummet in the stock market, and an intervention from Donald Trump. As Huang entered the company’s Silicon Valley office, wearing his signature dark-colored uniform, crowds of employees rushed to greet him clapping, hollering and chanting: “Jensen, Jensen, Jensen!”
summary: Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO of Nvidia, the world’s most valuable chip company, on Monday. He entered the company’s Silicon Valley headquarters wearing his dark‑colored uniform and was met by crowds of employees who clapped, hollered and chanted his name.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Taiwan warns Canada against deeper China trade ties after Carney meets Xi
content: Taiwan warned Canada against deepening trade ties with China. The caution arrived days after Canadian trade minister John Carney met Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, where the two sides agreed to further tariff cuts. Canada is seeking new markets amid the trade conflict that President Trump has continued.
summary: Taiwan warned Canada not to deepen trade ties with China. The warning came days after Carney met President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, where they agreed to further tariff cuts as Canada looks for new markets amid Trump’s trade war.
author: Euronews

title: US intelligence chief warns of more tech outages as Delta hits fresh Atlanta failure
content: The US intelligence chief warned that more technology outages are likely as Delta suffered a fresh failure in Atlanta. The warning comes amid a growing series of failures that Americans are experiencing across air travel, Microsoft email services, major banks and the National Security Agency’s network.
summary: The US intelligence chief warned that more technology outages are likely as Delta experienced a fresh failure in Atlanta. The warning comes amid a growing run of failures affecting air travel, Microsoft email services, major banks and the National Security Agency's network.
author: Euronews

title: Iran vows all means to counter US Hormuz blockade after Trump's threat
content: Foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei called the blockade an "act of crime" a day after Trump said Iranian ships trying to break it would go "to the bottom of the sea".
summary: Iran vows all means to counter US Hormuz blockade after Trump's threat.
author: Euronews

title: EU military chief Seán Clancy warns Europe must close critical gaps as hybrid threats rise
content: General Seán Clancy, the EU military chief, warned that hybrid threats were escalating. He said Europe was better prepared to defend itself but must accelerate efforts to close critical military gaps, citing growing threats from Russia and uncertainty over US military commitments.
summary: General Seán Clancy said Europe is better prepared to defend itself but must speed up efforts to close critical military gaps. He warned that hybrid threats are escalating amid growing threats from Russia and uncertainty over US military commitments.
author: Euronews

title: Oleksandra Matviichuk: Ukraine war a fight of unmanned machines, AI, total transparency
content: Speaking with FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney, Nobel Peace Prize laureate Oleksandra Matviichuk, Director of the Centre for Civil Liberties, says that today's war in Ukraine "is a war of unmanned machines, AI, total transparency of the battlefield, mass drones attacks and long range weapons, and this means we have to rethink how to protect human beings".
summary: Oleksandra Matviichuk: Ukraine war a fight of unmanned machines, AI, total transparency.
author: France 24

title: Africa disappointed with COP31 outcome as Turkey summit fails to agree
content:
The COP31 climate summit held in Turkey concluded without an agreement, highlighting stark divisions among participants over fossil‑fuel use and climate‑finance commitments. The failure has left many African delegates disappointed, as the summit did not produce a unified plan to address their climate‑change concerns.

In a separate development, President Félix Tshisekedi of the Democratic Republic of Congo and President William Ruto of Kenya announced an agreement to restore diplomatic ties and strengthen regional cooperation. The leaders said the renewed partnership would focus on collaborative initiatives across their respective countries.

Meanwhile, parents in a South African township repurposed a discarded shipping container into a sensory room for their children. The project was undertaken to provide a supportive environment that helps children cope with sensory needs and improve their well‑being.
summary: The COP31 climate summit in Turkey failed to reach an agreement, highlighting deep divisions over fossil fuels and climate finance. Meanwhile, DR Congo's Félix Tshisekedi and Kenya's William Ruto agreed to restore relations and boost regional cooperation, and parents in a South African township converted a discarded shipping container into a sensory room.
author: France 24

title: NATO pledges space defence after reports Russia may launch nuclear satellite
content: NATO Secretary‑General Mark Rutte said on Monday that the alliance will defend against threats in space after being asked about German media reports that Russia may be preparing to launch a nuclear‑armed satellite. The reports, which cite unnamed German military and BND intelligence sources, claim Moscow is thought to be planning such a launch in the coming weeks, potentially giving it the ability to destroy other satellites. The story was reported by FRANCE 24’s Laurent Berstecher.
summary: NATO chief Mark Rutte said the alliance would defend against threats in space. His remarks followed German media reports, citing unnamed German military and BND sources, that Russia may be preparing to launch a nuclear‑armed satellite in the coming weeks.
author: France 24

title: 14 nations acknowledge ICJ ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya
content:
Fourteen countries from Europe, Africa and Oceania have formally acknowledged the International Court of Justice’s ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority, urging the nation to meet its obligations under international law. 

Separately, the United Kingdom announced sanctions against five senior Myanmar military figures and stated it would formally recognize the genocide.
summary: Fourteen countries from Europe, Africa and Oceania have acknowledged the International Court of Justice ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya minority and called on Myanmar to comply with its international law obligations. The United Kingdom announced sanctions on five senior Myanmar military figures and said it would formally recognise the genocide.
author: France 24

title: Zelensky urges four-way peace talks with Russia, Europe and US as soon as possible
content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has called for a new round of negotiations that would bring together Ukraine, Russia, the United States, and European leaders.  

He said Kyiv is ready to meet as early as Tuesday to discuss a four‑way peace dialogue.
summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is calling for a new round of negotiations that would involve Ukraine, Russia, the United States and European leaders. He says Kyiv is ready to meet as early as Tuesday.
author: France 24

title: US drone over Mexico helps capture drug lord Fausto Isidro Meza Flores
content: Mexican officials say the United States flew a surveillance drone over Mexican territory to help locate and capture one of the country's most wanted drug traffickers. The operation led to the arrest of Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as 'El Chapo Isidro'.
summary: US drone over Mexico helps capture drug lord Fausto Isidro Meza Flores.
author: France 24

title: Trump praises Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO amid partisan scrutiny
content: US President Donald Trump praised Nvidia’s decision Monday to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive. The move sparked mixed reactions in Washington: Democratic leaders vowed investigations, while prominent Republicans questioned whether Huang’s return posed a national security risk.
summary: US President Donald Trump praised Nvidia's decision on Monday to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive. Democratic leaders vowed investigations and prominent Republicans questioned whether his return posed a national security risk.
author: France 24

title: UN Secretary-General Guterres decries COP31 collapse, calls for climate justice in Barbados
content: Secretary‑General António Guterres said on Sunday that he was deeply disappointed by the collapse of the COP31 climate negotiations. During a visit to Barbados, he called for stronger action on fossil fuels, increased climate finance and greater support for vulnerable nations.
summary: Secretary-General António Guterres said he was deeply disappointed by the collapse of the COP31 climate negotiations. During his visit to Barbados he urged stronger action on fossil fuels, increased climate finance and greater support for vulnerable nations.
author: UN News

title: UNSMIL calls for independent probe of Benghazi port and coastal attacks
content:
The UN Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL) has called for an independent investigation.  

The attacks were carried out at Benghazi port and off the coast of the eastern city on Sunday.
summary: The UN Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL) has called for an independent investigation into attacks at Benghazi port. The attacks also occurred off the coast of the eastern city on Sunday.
author: UN News

title: Heavy fighting near Ituri hospital disrupts DRC Ebola responders, forces 24‑hour cover
content: The World Health Organization reported that heavy fighting near a hospital in Ituri province of the Democratic Republic of the Congo has disrupted the work of Ebola responders. The conflict forced emergency teams to take cover for more than 24 hours.
summary: Heavy fighting near a hospital in Ituri province in the Democratic Republic of the Congo disrupted the work of Ebola responders. The emergency teams were forced to take cover for more than 24 hours.
author: UN News

title: Security Council meets on Russian attacks on Ukraine's grid and Black Sea grain shipments
content: The Security Council convened a high‑stakes meeting on Monday to address the impact of Russian attacks on Ukraine’s energy grid, which are leaving civilians without heat, power and water as winter begins. The session also examined how strikes on Black Sea shipping are endangering grain supplies for import‑dependent countries far from the conflict’s front lines.
summary: The Security Council held a high‑stakes meeting on Monday to discuss Russian attacks on Ukraine’s energy grid that have left civilians without heat, power and water. The council also examined how strikes on Black Sea shipping threaten grain supplies to import‑dependent countries far from the war’s frontline.
author: UN News

title: UN chief urges talks on global AI safety framework, warns of historic power shift
content: UN Secretary-General António Guterres on Monday called on Member States to begin discussions on a multilateral framework for managing the risks of artificial intelligence (AI), warning that the technology is driving “the biggest transfer of power in the history of humankind”.
summary: UN Secretary‑General António Guterres called on Member States to begin discussions on a multilateral framework for managing AI risks. He warned that the technology is driving the biggest transfer of power in the history of humankind.
author: UN News

title: UN deputy chief says Gaza war erases 77 years of development, calls for two‑State support
content: The United Nations warned that the Gaza war has erased 77 years of human development. On Monday, the UN deputy chief called for renewed international backing of a two‑State solution, noting that Palestinians still endure violence, displacement and dire living conditions even after the October 2025 ceasefire in Gaza.
summary: The UN deputy chief warned that the Gaza war has undone 77 years of human development and that Palestinians continue to face violence, displacement and dire living conditions. He urged renewed international support for a two‑State solution to the Israel‑Palestine conflict despite the October 2025 ceasefire in Gaza.
author: UN News

title: Gisèle Pelicot shocked as nude photos used to promote psychoanalyst book
content:
French activist Gisèle Pelicot, 73, announced she will pursue legal action against a publisher and author after nude photographs of her were used without consent to promote a psychoanalyst’s book. Pelicot said she is “deeply shocked” by the images and by the book’s suggestion that she was complicit in her own abuse.

Pelicot rose to international prominence in 2024 when a trial convicted her former husband of drugging and raping her and of enlisting 49 other men to rape her while she was unconscious. The case made her a global icon in the fight against sexual violence.
summary: Gisèle Pelicot shocked as nude photos used to promote psychoanalyst book.
author: Guardian World

title: Andy Burnham says rejoining EU without a referendum would be unthinkable
content:
Andy Burnham said it would be “unthinkable” for the United Kingdom to re‑join the European Union without holding another referendum, pledging to consult the public directly if he decides the country should return. He framed the stance as his strongest commitment yet to a public vote on any future EU membership.

The prime minister said former Tory premiers who have criticised the renewed Brexit debate are “stuck in the past”. He also announced plans to set out long‑term options for closer ties with the EU next month, with concrete steps to follow after the next general election, while pledging to adhere to Labour’s manifesto red lines.
summary: Andy Burnham says rejoining EU without a referendum would be unthinkable.
author: Guardian World

title: Dutch cycling culture faces challenges from e‑bikes, screens and declining civility
content: Awareness campaign reminds public ‘traffic is a team sport’ amid less civility and more collisions on roads For decades the Netherlands has been famed for its proud cycling culture, with a network of 23,000 miles of bike paths used by everyone from children under eight to adults over 80. In recent years, however, like so many countries around the world, it has seen a dramatic change in the type of vehicles using those lanes: no longer the preserve of pedal bikes, they are used by all manner of two-wheeled vehicles including electric cargo bikes, thick-tyred “fatbikes”, speed pedelecs, electric scooters and even some micro cars.
summary: An awareness campaign urges the public that “traffic is a team sport” as collisions rise and manners slip on Dutch bike lanes. The Netherlands’ 23,000‑mile network, once dominated by pedal bikes, now sees electric cargo bikes, fat‑bikes, speed pedelecs, e‑scooters and micro‑cars sharing the paths.
author: Guardian World

title: Beau Lamarre-Condon pleads not guilty to February 2024 Paddington murders, testifies
content: Former police officer has pleaded not guilty to murders of Jesse Baird and Luke Davies in Baird’s Paddington home in February 2024 Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Beau Lamarre-Condon could have sat in silence and let the crown “do its worst”, but he made the choice to take the “long walk” to the witness box, a jury has been told. Lamarre-Condon is accused of fatally shooting Jesse Baird and his partner, Luke Davies, with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024.
summary: Beau Lamarre-Condon pleads not guilty to February 2024 Paddington murders, testifies.
author: Guardian World

title: Australia to allow 5% global revenue fines on social media after Labor‑Greens pact
content:
Australia’s Labor Party and the Greens are working together on new online‑safety legislation that would allow individuals to sue big‑tech firms for online harm. The compromise deal creates a “digital duty of care” framework under which social‑media companies could face fines of up to 5 % of their global revenue, described as potentially “multibillion‑dollar” penalties. The Greens have agreed to back the bill after securing major amendments from Labor.

The legislation also includes provisions that, from late 2027, will let Australians opt out of addictive online algorithms and could end the “endless scroll” feature of social‑media feeds. Individuals will be able to bring court actions against platforms under the new rules.
summary: The compromise deal lets Australians sue big tech firms for online harm and could impose fines of up to 5% of a company's global revenue. The legislation, supported by Labor and the Greens, also lets users opt out of algorithmic feeds from late 2027 and may end endless scrolling.
author: Guardian World

title: China sentences official surnamed Ma to death for spying for foreign intelligence
content: A government‑linked publisher has reported that a Chinese official identified only by the surname Ma has been sentenced to death for espionage. According to Gold Wall Press, which is associated with China’s national administration of state secrets protection, Ma was recruited by an unnamed foreign intelligence service while he was working abroad. The publication says Ma leaked national secrets to an unnamed country and received payments exceeding $150,000 for the disclosures.
summary: A Chinese official surnamed Ma was sentenced to death for spying for an unnamed foreign intelligence service. He allegedly leaked national secrets and received payments of over $150,000, the government-linked Gold Wall Press reported.
author: Guardian World

title: South Korea orders Ulleungdo residents to shelter after Russian aircraft approach
content:
South Korean authorities ordered residents of the remote island of Ulleungdo to take shelter on Tuesday morning after several Russian military aircraft entered the nation’s air‑defence identification zone over the island and came close to its airspace. The military issued a pre‑emptive alert, anticipating a possible violation.

The defence ministry said it would summon the Russian defence attaché on Tuesday afternoon to lodge a strong protest over the incident.
summary: Residents of the South Korean island of Ulleungdo were ordered to take shelter after several Russian military aircraft entered the country's air defence identification zone over the island. The defence ministry said it would summon the Russian defence attaché that afternoon to lodge a strong protest.
author: Guardian World

title: Donald Trump impersonator Mark Critch mocks president at Ottawa press dinner
content:
At a parliamentary press gallery dinner in Ottawa on Saturday, Canada’s prime minister Mark Carney watched as a Donald Trump impersonator entered the stage. The comedian, Mark Critch, known for playing the former president on the sketch show This Hour Has 22 Minutes, appeared in a coiffed hairdo and an ill‑fitting suit.  

Critch danced onto the stage and lampooned the U.S. leader’s trade war and his alleged threats to annex Canada, while also joking about the president’s interest in men’s backsides. The remarks drew raucous laughter from a crowd of politicians and journalists in attendance.
summary: Comedian Mark Critch, who portrays Donald Trump on the sketch show This Hour Has 22 Minutes, appeared on stage at a parliamentary press gallery dinner in Ottawa. He lampooned the trade war Trump started and the president’s threats to annex Canada, drawing laughter from politicians and journalists while Canada’s prime minister Mark Carney watched.
author: Guardian World

title: Brainstorm Night Sky projector inspires dark‑sky trip plan
content:
The Brainstorm Night Sky projector, aimed at budding astronomers eight years old and up, sparked a personal revelation for the reviewer. After unboxing the device, the author noted the projector’s simplicity: a single button activates a circular image that can be tilted and focused, and a second press initiates a smooth, one‑speed rotation. The unit is lightweight, weighing 14.8 oz (420 g), and runs on three AA batteries that are not included. It projects up to 8.2 ft (2.5 m) wide and automatically turns off after 30 minutes, a feature that cannot be disabled.

The reviewer tested the blue version, which contains four interchangeable slides housed in protective cases. The slides include a moon, a solar system, and two depictions of the Northern Hemisphere’s night sky as seen from Hawaii—one with labeled constellations and one without. The projected images are described as crisp, with spherical planets that do not distort, and the projector’s rotation creates a hypnotic effect. The author praised the educational value of the first two slides and expressed frustration that Pluto’s demotion in 2006 is still reflected in the display.

A key moment in the review came when the reviewer inserted the slide showing Hawaii’s starry sky. The projected view, featuring over 20,000 stars according to Brainstorm, revealed a level of detail far beyond what the author could see from their own backyard, where light pollution limits visibility to 10–20 stars. This contrast motivated the reviewer to plan a trip to a dark‑sky site, noting that while smart telescopes can mitigate light pollution, the most effective solution is to travel away from skyglow. The reviewer is already researching local dark‑sky locations and considering binoculars for future stargazing.

The reviewer also highlighted limitations. The projector’s slide collection is fixed: the blue model offers four slides, the gray model six, and only one additional Southern Hemisphere slide can be purchased, capping the total at seven images. The slides are not interchangeable with those from the Brainstorm Deep Sky Projector. While the projector’s image quality and affordability (starting at $49.99) make it a solid educational tool, the lack of expandability and the 30‑minute sleep timer may reduce long‑term appeal. Nevertheless, the device successfully inspired the reviewer to pursue real‑world stargazing, raising the question of how much a plane ticket to Hawaii might cost.
summary: I didn’t expect much as I unboxed the Brainstorm Night Sky; after all, I’m significantly older than this educational star projector’s target audience. Perhaps I’d come away with a sense of wonder and delight, coupled with mild irritation at having to hunt down three AA batteries to power it.
author: Space.com

title: ESA's Mars Express captures image of ancient Tharsis Tholus volcano
content:
An image of Tharsis Tholus, a volcano on Mars, was captured by the European Space Agency’s Mars Express orbiter. The photo, produced by the spacecraft’s High‑Resolution Stereo Camera, shows the long‑dead volcano from orbit and is credited to ESA/DLR/FU Berlin.

Tharsis Tholus rises to about 4.97 miles (8 km), a height comparable to some of the tallest peaks in the Himalayan range. Although impressive, the volcano is only medium‑sized for Mars; the planet’s largest volcano, Olympus Mons, reaches roughly 13.2 miles (21.3 km) in height.

The volcano’s steepness is notable. Tharsis Tholus is steeper than Earth’s Mauna Kea, and the image’s vertical scale was exaggerated by researchers to highlight its topography in three dimensions, as reported by ESA.

Surface details reveal a history of impacts and erosion. The volcano’s flank is speckled with small holes that are craters from asteroid impacts, and the image shows cracks and other imperfections. These features, along with ancient lava flows that built up material, illustrate how erosion, warping, and impacts have reshaped the structure over time.

Studying such volcanoes allows scientists to reconstruct Mars’s ancient environment. By examining craters, cliffs, and worn surfaces, researchers can infer the planet’s past activity and its interaction with the surrounding landscape.
summary: ESA's Mars Express orbiter captured new high‑resolution imagery of the ancient volcano Tharsis Tholus on Mars. The volcano, about 4.97 miles tall and steeper than Earth’s Mauna Kea, shows craters, cracks, and erosion that reveal the planet’s past.
author: Space.com

title: Avengers: Doomsday drops final trailer showing Steve Rogers' return and X‑Men clash
content:
The latest “final trailer” for Avengers: Doomsday has been released by Disney and Marvel Studios, placing the spotlight on Steve Rogers. The film promises a larger‑scale spectacle than previous MCU releases since the Infinity Saga, with the trailer showing Rogers—no longer Captain America but still capable of wielding Mjolnir—alongside Thor as veteran leaders of the New Avengers.

The trailer also introduces a roster of allies that includes former colleagues, the Fantastic Four, and Fox’s X‑Men after a brief first‑encounter clash. A notable moment is Cyclops, played by James Marsden, delivering a line that is expected to excite X‑Men fans. The multiverse‑spanning plot remains largely hidden, but the trailer hints at the emotional stakes for Rogers and the way these heroes might cooperate against the film’s central threat.

Additional footage shows the mysterious Latverian witches, a detail that has fueled online speculation, and a poster for Doctor Doom that echoes an original Iron Man design. Kevin Feige has dismissed the idea that this version of Victor Von Doom is a Tony Stark variant.

Avengers: Doomsday is scheduled to open in cinemas on December 18, 2026, the same day as Dune: Part Three. The film will be available exclusively in theaters. For those following the MCU on Disney+, subscription options include Disney+ (With Ads) at $11.99 per month, Disney+ Premium (No Ads) at $18.99 per month or $189.99 per year.
summary: The final trailer for Avengers: Doomsday spotlights Steve Rogers, now wielding Mjolnir, and shows the New Avengers, Fantastic Four, and X‑Men fighting Victor Von Doom. It hints at a multiverse‑spanning conflict, reveals Rogers' emotional stakes, and notes the film’s December 18, 2026 cinema release, opening the same day as Dune: Part Three.
author: Space.com

title: Weird 'potato chips' and 'ghostly rocks' on Mars spotted by NASA rovers Curiosity and Perseverance
content:
NASA’s Curiosity and Perseverance rovers have recently documented a series of unusual Martian formations that scientists believe could shed light on the planet’s ancient environments. The discoveries, made in the “Nazca” and “Idubi” areas, include disk‑shaped crystal formations, bright silica‑rich rocks, and polygon‑shaped bedrock patterns.

At the Nazca drill site, Curiosity finished a drilling campaign and used its Mars Hand Lens Imager (MAHLI) to capture close‑up images of thin, flattened crystal formations embedded in the surrounding bedrock. The shapes resemble potato chips, a comparison made by the mission team. The rover also employed its ChemCam instrument to analyze the rocks’ chemical composition, and samples from the drill were delivered to the onboard Sample Analysis at Mars (SAM) instrument for further study.

In the “Idubi” region outside Jezero Crater, Perseverance photographed unusually bright, pale rocks on Oct. 29, 2026 (Sol 2023) with its left Mastcam‑Z camera. SuperCam data showed that these formations are rich in hydrated silica rather than typical igneous material. Hydrated silica on Earth can form in hydrothermal or groundwater settings and can preserve microscopic fossils, making these Martian deposits of particular interest to life‑search scientists.

Curiosity also captured polygon‑shaped patterns outlined by raised ridges on Nov. 13, 2026 (Sol 5073) using its Mast Camera (Mastcam). The patterns, similar to those seen earlier on Mount Sharp’s slopes, may result from mineral shrinkage during water evaporation, temperature changes, or the expansion and compaction of buried sediments. By studying the composition of the rocks and the cementing material around the ridges, researchers aim to determine which processes shaped the terrain.

Together, these observations illustrate how the rovers’ detailed imaging and analytical tools are revealing subtle geological features that record Mars’ climatic and hydrologic history. As Curiosity continues its ascent of Mount Sharp and Perseverance investigates ancient terrains beyond Jezero Crater, the missions are piecing together a more comprehensive picture of the Red Planet’s complex geological past.
summary: Weird 'potato chips' and 'ghostly rocks' on Mars spotted by NASA rovers Curiosity and Perseverance.
author: Space.com

title: Blue Origin achieves first vertical landing from space with New Shepard rocket
content:
On November 23, 2015, Blue Origin achieved the first successful vertical landing from space with its suborbital New Shepard rocket. Prior to this event, all rockets were single-use, including those operated by SpaceX. The New Shepard capsule launched safely into space before the rocket began its return to Earth. It flew toward a landing pad, reignited its engine to slow down, and touched down softly on the ground. This milestone demonstrated that rockets could be reused for multiple missions, a development intended to save money and reduce waste.

The success of the New Shepard landing initiated an era of vertical launch and landing for rockets. While SpaceX later became well-known for landing Falcon 9 boosters from orbit and catching Starship megarockets with metal arms, Blue Origin was the first to accomplish a vertical landing from space. Since the initial 2015 landing, Blue Origin has conducted 38 New Shepard missions between April 2015 and 2026, comprising 17 suborbital astronaut flights and 21 uncrewed flights. The company repeatedly reused its New Shepard boosters, although it lost one during an uncrewed launch following a technical issue.

In January 2026, Blue Origin announced a two-year pause in New Shepard flights to focus on moon lander projects. The company continued its focus on rocket landings by integrating vertical landing capabilities into its larger orbital rocket, New Glenn. New Glenn achieved its first successful landing in 2025, nearly ten years after the initial New Shepard touchdown. Blue Origin has since reflown a New Glenn booster and is developing a new rocket engine named Northstar for improved performance.
summary: On Nov. 23, 2015, Blue Origin's New Shepard rocket made the first successful vertical landing from space. The event marked the beginning of reusable rocket technology, allowing Blue Origin to conduct 38 missions between 2015 and 2026.
author: Space.com

title: Space.com Launches Free Giveaway for Two Dwarflab Mini Smart Telescopes
content:
Space.com’s Community team has launched a giveaway exclusively for Space+ members, offering a chance to win one of two Dwarflab mini smart telescopes. Each telescope is valued at $419. The promotion is open to U.S. residents only and runs through January 4, 2027. To enter, individuals must sign up for the free Space.com Plus (Space+) club membership by providing their email address on the contest entry page, where the rules and eligibility requirements are listed. Existing Space+ members can also participate by entering the email associated with their membership.

Space+ is a free membership program designed for space enthusiasts. Members can unlock badges for reading Space.com articles, play space-themed games, and take cosmic quizzes. Additionally, subscribers can sign up for Space.com newsletters to receive updates on space news, discoveries, and skywatching events. This Dwarflab smart telescope giveaway is the first contest for the program, though the team notes it will not be the last.

The Dwarflab Mini is an ultra-compact 30-mm refractor telescope described as one of the most portable smart telescopes available. It is positioned as an affordable entry-level option for stargazers interested in smart telescope astrophotography. Winners will be announced in January 2027 via the contest page, with two U.S. winners selected in total.
summary: Space.com Launches Free Giveaway for Two Dwarflab Mini Smart Telescopes.
author: Space.com

title: Writer praises Coming to America as a feelgood comfort film
content:
In a new installment of a series where writers select their most rewatched comfort films, an author highlights Eddie Murphy’s comedy “Coming to America” as a feelgood movie that reminds them of home. The piece opens by describing a memorable scene in which Murphy’s character, Prince Akeem, stands on a balcony in a Queens neighborhood. Dressed in a tailored jacket and red tie, the prince with a foreign accent misunderstands a hostile shout from a neighbor below as a greeting, illustrating the film’s central theme of cultural clash.

The article outlines the plot, noting that Prince Akeem is the sole heir to the throne of the fictitious African country of Zamunda. Rejecting an arranged marriage, he uses a coin flip and a personal globe to choose Queens, New York, as the location to find his own bride. Accompanied by his sidekick Semmi, Akeem attempts to assimilate into the fast pace of New York life. His target is Lisa, the heiress to the McDowell’s fast-food business, who is already engaged to another man.

To get closer to Lisa, Akeem conceals his royal identity and takes a job at her father’s restaurant. The writer poses questions about whether Akeem and Lisa will fall in love while he poses as a working-class employee, and whether Lisa will leave her arrogant fiancé. The piece concludes with a spoiler alert indicating a happy ending, praising the film for its simple plot progression and character development that is described as full of heart and candor.
summary: The article highlights Eddie Murphy's performance as Prince Akeem in the culture-clash comedy Coming to America. It describes the plot where the prince travels to Queens to find a bride and works at a fast-food restaurant to win over his love interest.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Theaster Gates takes over America's last porcelain factory, Pickard China
content:
Theaster Gates, a celebrated artist, is investing in the Pickard China factory, a 60,000-square-foot brick building located just outside of Chicago. Gates describes the acquisition as a fight to demand that humans are worth investing in and aims to bring “independent thinking” back to fine china. The facility is currently the last operational porcelain fine china factory in the United States.

Inside the entrance, a 1910 advertisement highlights the factory’s historical emphasis on craftsmanship, noting that most of its artists were trained in European art centers and that each piece was painted from start to finish by the same master craftsman. Today, the factory is in a state of disrepair, with its 12 remaining employees working to fulfill longstanding orders. These clients include the White House, which has used Pickard china since 2008, as well as Williams Sonoma, US embassies, private golf clubs, and private customers.
summary: Theaster Gates is investing in the 60,000 sq ft Pickard China factory, described as the last operational porcelain fine china factory in the US. The facility, located just outside Chicago, is in disrepair with 12 remaining employees fulfilling orders for the White House and other clients.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Blade Runner 2099 debuts on Prime Video
content:
Blade Runner 2099 is a new sci‑fi sequel that debuted on Prime Video this Wednesday, expanding the franchise that has long been a fan favourite. The series is part of a broader trend of turning established film properties into television shows, a strategy that has been applied to franchises such as Harry Potter, Lord of the Rings, Alien and Star Wars.  

The author of the piece, a long‑time fan of the original Blade Runner films, notes that the earlier movie presented a future where technology has taken over every aspect of life, yet inequality, surveillance, artificial beings and unchecked corporate power have worsened. The new Amazon‑produced series is said to continue that vision, though the writer expresses uncertainty about its clarity and direction.  

The article also questions why a high‑profile franchise like James Bond, which is co‑owned by Amazon, has not yet been adapted into a television series, suggesting that the decision to bring Blade Runner 2099 to Prime Video may be a strategic move to tap into the lucrative franchise‑mining market.
summary: Blade Runner 2099 is a new series expansion that premiered on Amazon Prime Video from Wednesday. The writer, a fan of the original films, reflects on how the series expands the Blade Runner universe.
author: Guardian Culture

title: IDFA 2026 features 250+ documentaries on global conflict
content:
The International Documentary Film Festival Amsterdam (IDFA) is set to showcase a lineup of over 250 documentaries, positioning non-fiction cinema for a potential breakthrough in audience reach. The festival, described as the world’s largest documentary event, takes place in Amsterdam’s downtown district near the torture museum. It serves as a contrast to the fictional dramas and celebrity-focused events of other major film festivals, offering a focus on crisis, resistance, and human kindness.

Recent successes in the genre, including films titled Musk, NAZA, and You Can See Everything, have attracted large audiences, suggesting a growing appetite for non-fiction storytelling. The upcoming IDFA program explores various geopolitical hotspots, featuring narratives of forced displacement in the West Bank and Gaza. The festival’s opening night film, White Tiger Column, focuses on a jungle-based guerrilla army in Myanmar, while Carol Nguyen’s Still Night, Burning House addresses the experiences of traumatised children from the Vietnamese boat people community.

Beyond current headlines, the festival highlights stories that have previously remained out of public view. Raluca Lupascu’s A Modern Roma Fairytale is cited as a gripping kitchen-sink tragedy that brings attention to overlooked narratives. The event aims to keep viewers informed and engaged with the realities depicted in these documentaries, ranging from global conflicts to intimate personal stories.
summary: The International Documentary Film Festival Amsterdam (IDFA) in 2026 screened over 250 documentaries, including films on the West Bank, Gaza, Myanmar, and Vietnamese boat people. The festival, held in Amsterdam's downtown district near the torture museum, offers a sharp counterpoint to the drama and pageantry of Cannes, Toronto, and Venice.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Ariana Grande, Stiller, De Niro Join 4th “Focker In‑Law” Comedy
content:
A review of the fourth "Focker In-Law" film describes it as a 90s-style grossout comedy that suffers from a depressing sense of overfamiliarity. The article notes that even Ariana Grande’s talent cannot save the movie, which is part of a modern Hollywood franchise characterized as consistently moderate but lucrative. The review highlights that the series often features heavyweight actors, including Dustin Hoffman, Barbra Streisand, and Harvey Keitel, who appear uncertain about their roles.

The writer specifically questions Robert DeNiro’s performance, stating he does not seem to be completely on top of the material. This perceived distraction is described as a recurring issue, as DeNiro has given the same impression in the previous three films in the franchise.
summary: The film is the fourth entry in the franchise and features Ariana Grande, Stiller, and Robert De Niro. The reviewer describes it as a 90s‑style grossout cringe comedy that feels overfamiliar and says De Niro appears distracted.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Steven Spielberg to Direct Paul Thomas Anderson's Western The Heart in Winter
content: Steven Spielberg has announced his next project will be a western scripted by Paul Thomas Anderson. The two Oscar-winning filmmakers are set to collaborate on an adaptation of Kevin Barry’s 2024 novel, The Heart in Winter. Jessie Buckley, Cillian Murphy, and Mark Rylance are reportedly set to star in the film.
summary: Steven Spielberg will direct a western adapted from Kevin Barry's 2024 novel, The Heart in Winter. The film is scripted by Paul Thomas Anderson and reportedly stars Jessie Buckley, Cillian Murphy, and Mark Rylance.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Amazon’s Christmas romcom Clashing Through the Snow is a bust
content:
Amazon’s latest holiday romantic comedy, Clashing Through the Snow, has received a negative review, described as a "bust" that fails to justify its chaotic cross-country premise. The film stars Christopher Briney, known for The Summer I Turned Pretty, and Michelle Randolph, who appeared in 1923. The review notes that while the actors give their best effort, the movie does not live up to expectations.

The story begins with a self-aware critique of the publishing industry, where boutique press head Jeremy, played by PJ Byrne, announces New Year’s layoffs. The narrative follows two Los Angeles-based editors, Ryan and Hannah, who are rivals at work. Both are tasked with finding a massive book deal within a week to secure their positions. Despite the industry’s current state, the characters embark on a journey to New York for meetings, setting the stage for the film’s holiday romance plot.
summary: Clashing Through the Snow follows Amazon star Christopher Briney and 1923 actress Michelle Randolph as they race to secure a blockbuster book amid industry layoffs. The review calls the film a bust, noting the chaotic cross‑country journey is not worth taking.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Racing Post to drop greyhound racecards from print edition
content: Latest greyhound racing blow is a wake-up call with new five-year plan keeping RSPCA on side for now Britain’s greyhound racing industry woke up on Monday to the news that the Racing Post, the daily trade newspaper that has carried extensive coverage of the sport since its launch in 1986, will drop both editorial and greyhound racecards in its print edition from 10 December. In a letter to Racing Post readers, Tom Kerr, its editor, said that it had been an “immensely difficult decision” and blamed “tax rises that have hit betting shops [which] have put pressure on the whole industry,” adding that “like other businesses, we have to make hard choices about where we focus our resources.” Five members of staff are expected to lose their jobs as a result of the decision.
summary: Racing Post will remove both editorial and greyhound racecards from its print edition starting 10 December. Editor Tom Kerr said the decision was difficult and blamed tax rises on betting shops, with five staff expected to lose their jobs.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Max Verstappen Criticises Overtake-Heavy Las Vegas Grand Prix
content:
Max Verstappen has criticized the Las Vegas Grand Prix, stating that the race “isn’t how it should be” for Formula One. The Red Bull driver described the event as not true to the spirit of the sport, despite securing a victory in Nevada. The race was characterized by cars slipstreaming each other, leading to a high volume of position changes.

Verstappen’s win came after the lead changed hands 35 times during the competition. He noted that he had to defend his lead and retake it repeatedly throughout the event. The race in Nevada featured a total of 352 overtakes, a statistic Verstappen used to highlight his concerns about the racing format.
summary: Red Bull driver Max Verstappen said his victory at the Las Vegas Grand Prix was not true to the spirit of Formula One. The race featured 352 overtakes, with Verstappen defending and retaking his lead after it changed hands 35 times in a slipstream-dominated contest.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Mauricio Pochettino can now see just how desperate Manchester United are | Jonathan Wilson
content:
Mauricio Pochettino’s debut as manager of Manchester United ended in a heavy defeat, underscoring the urgency for a morale lift within the squad if the club is to escape a looming relegation fight. The match, played away at Liverpool, was not expected to be a decisive test of the new coach, yet the outcome made it clear that the team’s situation is dire.

The game began with a dramatic early blow: Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes, leaving United to play the majority of the match with ten men. Despite United’s historic win at Anfield last season—their first there in a decade—the loss of a player made the task of maintaining a competitive edge even more difficult. United fell behind 2‑0 by the 13th minute, raising concerns that the defeat could resemble the 7‑0 loss to Liverpool in 2023.

Pochettino’s tactical switch to a back three brought a measure of stability, but the team still conceded 28 shots, 11 on target, and an expected goals (xG) figure of 4.38. Liverpool’s 18 shots in the 2019‑20 fixture, eight of them on target, are dwarfed by the Sunday performance, illustrating the extent of the defeat. While some credit can be given for the narrow 4‑0 scoreline, the magnitude of the loss suggests that United could have suffered a much larger margin.

The match has highlighted the pressing need for Pochettino to rally a demoralised squad and reverse the downward trend that threatens to drag the club into a relegation battle.
summary: Mauricio Pochettino can now see just how desperate Manchester United are | Jonathan Wilson.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Emery says no change to Villa's Champions League plan despite Galatasaray pitch concerns
content: ‘Hopefully the pitch will be as best as possible,’ says Villa manager Turkish champions had to move game on Saturday Unai Emery has insisted he will not alter his plans for Aston Villa’s Champions League game at ­Galatasaray on Tuesday night on account of concerns about the state of the pitch. The Turkish champions hastily moved Saturday’s home fixture from Rams Park after starting emergency repairs to the surface this month. The Villa defender Ian Maatsen said he and his teammates were aware the pitch was in a “bad condition”. Villa were informed by Uefa last week that they would be unable to train at the venue the day before the Champions League game in order to give the pitch maximum time to recover after heavy maintenance work. Galatasaray played Saturday’s victory over Samsunspor at Basaksehir Fatih Terim stadium, a significantly smaller ground named after the former Turkey manager, who played for and managed Galatasaray.
summary: Emery says no change to Villa's Champions League plan despite Galatasaray pitch concerns.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Infantino’s World Cup sell‑off plan could lock football for up to 96 years, documents show
content:
Documents reviewed by the Guardian reveal that FIFA President Gianni Infantino’s failed “Fifa Forward Enterprise” plan would have committed the sport to a 96-year term. The proposal, which sought to sell off football’s commercial assets, was designed to generate profits from the sport’s growing revenues for nearly a century. Communications between FIFA and Thrive Capital, the lead investor, indicate the scheme was finalized days before the 2026 World Cup final.

Under the plan, the management team was positioned to receive payouts of up to 5% of the enterprise’s multi-billion-pound value. Although FIFA denies that Infantino would have personally profited from the arrangement, the previously undisclosed communications highlight the significant financial incentives for the organization’s leadership. The failed initiative aimed to leverage the sport’s burgeoning commercial landscape through a long-term partnership with its primary investor.
summary: Infantino’s World Cup sell‑off plan could lock football for up to 96 years, documents show.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Nations Championship finals weekend to start with 40,000 empty seats at Twickenham
content:
The inaugural Nations Championship finals weekend will begin on Friday with the opening night played in front of roughly 40,000 empty seats, as the top tier of the Allianz Stadium in Twickenham is closed. Organisers report that ticket sales are strong, with 70 % of seats already taken.

Despite the high demand, more than half of the tickets for the 82,000‑capacity venue remain available for the Ireland v Australia/Italy v Fiji double‑header, according to The Guardian. The figure could rise further now that organisers have opened a ticket‑swap exchange for fans wishing to watch their team.
summary: Nations Championship finals weekend to start with 40,000 empty seats at Twickenham.
author: Guardian Sport

title: 2035 Women’s World Cup awarded to England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland
content: The 2035 Women’s World Cup will be hosted across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, marking the first confirmed bid after the United Kingdom emerged as the sole applicant. Organisers stress that maximising the tournament’s societal impact—particularly the fight against misogyny—should be a top priority. While the UK’s exclusive bid meant the outcome was expected, officials say the submission was neither complacent nor lacking ambition, and they hope the event can deliver a massive societal benefit for women and girls throughout the country.
summary: The 2035 Women’s World Cup will be hosted in England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland after the UK was the sole bidder. Organisers say maximising the tournament’s societal impact, including combating misogyny, should be a top priority.

content:
A live minute‑by‑minute update is available for the 8 pm UK kick‑off of the Premier League match between Brentford and Everton. The commentary notes that “Haaland must be worried” and references Moyes’s comments on Thierno Barry. content: Former world champion Deontay Wilder is scheduled to fight heavyweight Martin Bakole on the undercard of Tyson Fury versus Anthony Joshua in Cardiff on 11 December.
summary: Former world champion Deontay Wilder will fight heavyweight Martin Bakole on the undercard of Tyson Fury versus Anthony Joshua. The bout is scheduled for 11 December in Cardiff.

content: Kevin de Bruyne says he has "love" for Manchester City's owners and his feelings for the club will "never change" despite being found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial rules.

content:
The Department of Justice (DOJ) has stated in recent court filings that the administration deported a U.S. citizen to Mexico after officials mistakenly assumed he was an immigrant without legal status.  

In the filings, U.S. Attorney Justin R. Simmons noted that Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) had detained Brian José Morales García.

title: Trump to speak at DOJ, challenge Newsom over inmate commutations
content:
President Trump will speak at the Department of Justice on Monday, where he is expected to highlight his law‑and‑order agenda and criticize California Governor Gavin Newsom for commuting the death sentences of more than 548 inmates.  

His appearance comes as the DOJ sees a wave of departures following the midterm elections.
summary: President Trump will deliver remarks Monday at the Department of Justice. He is expected to tout his agenda and challenge California Gov. Gavin Newsom over the commutation of more than 548 death sentences.

title: Polymarket and Kalshi failed to beat mainstream forecasts in midterms, report says
content:
A new report released Monday by the Anti‑Corruption Data Collective found that a small group of sophisticated traders collected the vast majority of profits from bets on this month’s congressional midterm elections on Polymarket.  

The analysis also showed that thousands of ordinary bettors lost money.

title: Rep. Jimmy Gomez resigns from Congress after Ethics Committee finds sexual misconduct
content: Rep. Jimmy Gomez (D-Calif.) announced his resignation from Congress following a House Ethics Committee report that found “substantial evidence” of sexual misconduct. The report indicated Gomez engaged in “making unwelcome sexual advances and sexual contact” with a House staffer. In a Monday statement, Gomez acknowledged the “seriousness” of the committee’s findings.
summary: Rep. Jimmy Gomez (D-Calif.) said he was resigning from Congress after a House Ethics Committee report found “substantial evidence” that he had engaged in sexual misconduct, including “making unwelcome sexual advances and sexual contact” with a House staffer.

title: More than 700,000 Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine war, analysis shows
content: An analysis released Monday reports that more than 700,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in the conflict in Ukraine. The figure, derived from new data obtained from the Russian state statistics service, exceeds the number of U.S. casualties in all wars fought in the past 150 years combined.
summary: More than 700,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in Moscow’s war in Ukraine, according to an analysis released Monday. The figure was found using new data from the Russian state statistics service.

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang returns after board reversal amid pressure
content: Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia as CEO on Monday, prompting questions about how the board of directors reversed its decision within days. The board reportedly faced pressure from the Trump administration, Silicon Valley leaders, and slumping markets amid concerns regarding Nvidia’s future without Huang.
summary: Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia as CEO on Monday. The board reversed its decision within days amid pressure from the Trump administration, Silicon Valley leaders, and slumping markets.

title: Democrats flip 47 House seats as COP31 ends without a deal after record-long talks
content: Democrats have flipped 47 House seats, with the potential to reach 49, securing the largest margin in 50 years. Meanwhile, climate change negotiations at COP31 extended two days beyond the scheduled end, making it the longest conference in the summit's history, though it concluded without a deal.
summary: Democrats have flipped 47 House seats and could flip 49 total. COP31 concluded without a deal after talks ran two days longer than expected, becoming the longest conference in the summit’s history.
author: NPR Politics

title: Cop31 Fails to Reach Climate Pact, First Time in 17 Years
content:
The Guardian editorial criticizes the failure of the Cop31 summit in Turkey to reach a climate pact, marking the first such breakdown in 17 years. The publication argues that this failure should not be used as an excuse to maintain the damaging status quo, emphasizing that a credible route to agreement requires making commitments and seeking concessions, which did not occur during the weekend negotiations.

According to the editorial, the primary responsibility for the impasse lies with petrostates that resisted transitioning away from fossil fuels and wealthy nations that were unwilling to provide adequate financial support. The article notes that the United States was absent from the talks, while the European Union was the leading wealthy nation involved. Although the editorial supports the EU’s objection to fossil-fuel backsliding by a Saudi-Russian coalition, it criticizes European governments for ruling out new funding for climate action in developing countries.

The piece highlights that other parties, notably China and the African group, were prepared to accept a flawed package to preserve multilateralism, despite their reservations. The Guardian concludes that the climate crisis demands the next UN summit transform promises into action, rather than allowing the current lack of progress to persist.
summary: Petrostates blocked ambition while wealthy nations withheld cash support. The failure of Cop31 in Turkey to reach a climate pact, the first time this has happened in 17 years, was mainly due to petrostates resisting a transition away from fossil fuels and wealthy nations unwilling to finance it properly.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Golden mantella habitat targeted by illegal gold mining in Madagascar
content:
Albert Rakotoarisoa discovered forty holes dug into the marshy ground of the Mangabe reserve in eastern Madagascar, indicating recent illegal gold mining activity. He noted that the holes were absent when he visited the site just weeks prior, expressing disappointment over the visible damage to the area.

The presence of the golden mantella frog is associated with gold deposits, making its habitat a target for these mining operations. This activity is contributing to the destruction of fragile ecosystems across the country, positioning the rare amphibian as an ecological warning sign for Madagascar.
summary: The golden mantella's habitat in Madagascar is being targeted by illegal gold mining, damaging fragile ecosystems. Albert Rakotoarisoa observed 40 new holes in Mangabe reserve, noting they were absent a few weeks earlier and expressing disappointment.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Arctic air brings colder temperatures to Europe this week
content:
A warmer‑than‑average November has left the world’s surface temperatures above the pre‑industrial baseline, with the latest data showing the global mean 2.12 °C above that reference. The increase is the largest anomaly on record and the highest since the 1991‑2020 climate average, a trend that coincides with one of the strongest El Niño events ever recorded.

In contrast, parts of Europe are poised for a cold snap this week as Arctic air moves in. Meteorologists warn that temperatures across a large swathe of the continent could drop sharply, reversing the recent warmth that has been seen in the region.
summary: Arctic air brings colder temperatures to Europe this week.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Al Gore Leads Call for Reform After Cop31 Failure
content:
The failure to reach a keystone agreement at COP31 has prompted international climate diplomacy experts and scientists to call for urgent reform of the United Nations’ climate summits. Former U.S. vice‑president Al Gore is among the climate leaders demanding a change to the current consensus rule, arguing that the decision‑making process must be altered to achieve more decisive outcomes.  

The talks in Antalya, co‑chaired by Turkey and Australia, were intended to produce a sweeping pact that would inject urgency into global calls for climate action and provide support for countries most exposed to the crisis. The lack of such an agreement has highlighted the need for a new approach to how decisions are made at future UN climate summits.
summary: Former US vice‑president Al Gore is among climate leaders demanding a change to the consensus rule after the Antalya summit. The failure to reach a keystone agreement at Cop31 has exposed the need to reform how the UN’s climate summits make decisions, according to international climate diplomacy experts and scientists.
author: Guardian Environment

title: California Faces Potential Record Floods as High Tides Hit Thanksgiving Week
content: California’s coastal communities are bracing for a potential surge of flooding during Thanksgiving week. Officials report that a winter high‑tide event could combine with ongoing El Niño conditions to produce record‑breaking floods along the coast and inland. The state has already faced a difficult year, with residents experiencing flooding, extreme waves, and beach erosion during the super El Niño season. Experts warn that the upcoming travel week could bring additional havoc as cities prepare for possible historic flood conditions.
summary: Coastal California cities are preparing for possible historic floods that could coincide with El Niño conditions during the busy travel week. Experts warn that a winter high tide event could bring record‑breaking floods on the coast and inland during Thanksgiving week.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Family History Frequently Cited as Cancer Risk Factor by Friends
content: Many people recognize family history as a factor that can increase the risk of cancer. When asked to name three risk factors, most respondents include some version of “family history” on their lists. This common perception highlights the importance of understanding how genetics may influence cancer risk.
summary: People often name family history as a cancer risk factor. The article notes that most friends include it in their lists.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Yale Study Reveals How Sensory Neurons Guide Goal-Directed Behavior
content: A new Yale study offers insight into a fundamental question in neuroscience: how the nervous system transforms sensory information into signals that help us achieve our goals. The research explores how sensory neurons contribute to goal‑directed behavior.
summary: A Yale study examines how the nervous system converts sensory input into signals that guide goal attainment. The research addresses a fundamental neuroscience question.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Lack of Brazilian Data Hinders Accuracy of Heart Failure Genetic Tests
content: A study by the University of São Paulo (USP) found that Brazilians’ low representation in global genomic databases reduces the accuracy of genetic tests used to investigate heart‑failure causes. The research also showed that interpreting results is notably harder when analyzing DNA segments of African or Indigenous ancestry.
summary: A study by the University of São Paulo (USP) found that the low representation of Brazilians in global genomic databases compromises the accuracy of heart failure genetic tests. The study also noted that interpreting results is significantly more difficult when analyzing DNA segments of African or Indigenous ancestry.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Starting Small Today May Beat Big New Year's Resolutions
content: Millions of people annually set New Year's resolutions to lose weight, improve diet, and increase exercise, viewing January as a natural point for a fresh start. However, these large-scale commitments often generate significant pressure and prove difficult to maintain over time.
summary: Millions of people promise to lose weight, eat better, and exercise more each year. Big resolutions create a lot of pressure and are hard to keep up, so starting small today may be more effective than waiting until January.
author: Medical Xpress

title: University of Michigan study finds high school drug use linked to earlier adult death
content: A five‑decade University of Michigan study shows that high school students who smoke cigarettes, use cannabis, or take other drugs face a higher risk of dying earlier in adulthood.
summary: A five-decade University of Michigan study found that high schoolers who smoke cigarettes, use cannabis or take other drugs have a higher risk of dying earlier in adulthood. The research measured the long-term toll of high school substance use on mortality.
author: Medical Xpress

title: UTHealth researchers find visual system creates fear memories, halted by brain stimulation
content: Researchers at McGovern Medical School at UTHealth Houston have identified that the brain’s visual system actively converts threatening experiences into lasting fear memories. They also found that noninvasive brain stimulation can disrupt this transformation process.
summary: Researchers at McGovern Medical School at UTHealth Houston discovered that the brain's visual system actively transforms threatening experiences into lasting fear memories. They also found that noninvasive brain stimulation can interrupt this process.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Falklands oil plans threaten seals, whales and penguins
content:
The Falkland Islands, a British overseas territory claimed by Argentina, host significant oil reserves that are the subject of a sovereignty dispute between the two nations. Environmentalists express concern that these oil plans threaten one of the Atlantic’s richest ecosystems. The archipelago consists of East and West Falkland, along with 778 smaller islands and islets located east of Patagonia’s southern tip.

The region supports large colonies of albatrosses and penguins. Additionally, the waters surrounding the islands and the Patagonian shelf serve as feeding grounds for sea lions, southern elephant seals, and southern right whales.
summary: Environmentalists fear the Falklands oil plans could harm the islands' rich marine ecosystem. The Falklands, a British overseas territory claimed by Argentina, hosts large colonies of albatrosses, penguins, sea lions, southern elephant seals and southern right whales.
author: Guardian Business

title: US Thanksgiving Flights Hit by 18,000 Cancellations After FAA Ground Stop
content:
Millions of people are planning to fly in the United States for the Thanksgiving holiday, just two weeks after the Federal Aviation Administration implemented a nationwide ground stop on November 13. This event halted all flights for the first time since 9/11, excluding a brief halt in 2023. The disruption caused significant chaos, with some travelers driving overnight to reach cruise ships or purchasing new cars to attend business meetings, while others canceled their plans and incurred associated costs.

According to estimates from Anderson Economic Group, more than 18,000 flights were canceled during the incident. This resulted in a potential cost to travelers of $1.9 billion in lost time and related expenses. As the holiday travel period approaches, the article notes that travelers must navigate an outdated system and complex company policies in case of further disruptions, advising them to carry cash and know their rights.
summary: More than 18,000 flights were cancelled, costing travelers $1.9bn in lost time and expenses, according to Anderson Economic Group. The cancellations followed a 13 November FAA ground stop that halted all flights nationwide for the first time since 9/11.
author: Guardian Business

title: Global Stock Markets Volatile as AI Companies Face Sell-Offs
content:
Shares have been volatile amid growing jitters over technology and artificial‑intelligence companies. Investors are reportedly “getting cold feet” over the outlook for AI firms and are selling technology stocks, according to recent market reports.

Last week, the AI company Anthropic went public and recorded a record‑breaking first day on the exchange. However, on Friday global stock markets tumbled, and the U.S. Nasdaq closed 5 % below its previous level on 1 January.
summary: Global stock markets have seen rapid rallies and sharp sell-offs as investors grow wary of AI companies. The AI company Anthropic had a record-breaking first day after its launch, but markets fell and the US Nasdaq closed 5% lower on January 1.
author: Guardian Business

title: Nvidia Shares Close at $165.05 as CEO Jensen Huang Returns, Value Rises $950bn
content:
Nvidia’s market value surged by $950 billion after the company’s shares closed at $165.05, following the surprise reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang. The jump left the firm’s valuation still half a trillion dollars lower than before the affair was revealed.

President‑elect Donald Trump praised Huang, calling him a “great patriot and national treasure” in response to his return. The announcement generated widespread coverage in U.S. political circles, highlighting the CEO’s reinstatement as a key event in Nvidia’s recent timeline.

Meanwhile, UK housebuilder Crest Nicholson saw its shares fall by a quarter to a record low after issuing a profits warning. The company’s full‑year completions were 1,353, the bottom end of its guidance range of 1,350 to 1,400. The warning pushed Crest Nicholson shares down over 30%, dragging peers such as Barratt Redrow, Persimmon, Vistry and Bellway into the red. The downturn reflects broader weakness in the housing market, affecting not only first‑time buyers but also affluent upsizers amid macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty.
summary: Nvidia Shares Close at $165.05 as CEO Jensen Huang Returns, Value Rises $950bn.
author: Guardian Business

title: Chernobyl‑surviving fungus could aid creation of nerve‑agent‑trapping materials
content:
Scientists have identified a fungus that can thrive in the Chernobyl exclusion zone and may be used to develop materials capable of trapping and breaking down nerve agents and pesticides.  

Deep inside the zone, black molds climb the walls of the damaged former nuclear plant in Ukraine. They are undeterred by the high radiation levels and, in some cases, grow toward the radiation.
summary: A fungus that can survive in Chernobyl could help create materials that trap and break down nerve agents and pesticides. Black molds climb the walls of the damaged former nuclear plant in Ukraine and are undeterred by the radiation, some even growing toward it.
author: Phys.org

title: 40 Charred Papyrus Fragments Found in Thebes Reveal Widespread Curse Ritual
content:
A recent find of 40 charred papyrus fragments at a temple in the ancient city of Thebes has prompted scholars to rethink a well‑known ancient Egyptian curse ritual.  

The fragments suggest the ritual was far more widespread and commonplace than previously believed, altering researchers’ understanding of its historical reach.
summary: Researchers discovered 40 charred papyrus fragments at a temple in Thebes. The fragments suggest that the famous ancient Egyptian curse ritual was more widespread and commonplace than previously thought.
author: Phys.org

title: Automated AI pollen analysis matches conventional honey testing
content: A research team from the Helmholtz Centre for Environmental Research (UFZ) and the German Centre for Integrative Biodiversity Research (iDiv) in Leipzig has developed an automated, AI‑based pollen analysis method for honey testing. The method was created in collaboration with several partners and is designed to assess the pollen content of single‑flower honeys, which must contain a specific proportion of pollen from the plant that produced the nectar. According to the project’s findings, the automated analysis closely matches conventional testing, offering a faster and less expert‑dependent alternative for verifying honey authenticity.
