title: Russian strike on Dymer apartment building north of Kyiv kills two
content: A Russian attack on Sunday hit an apartment building in the village of Dymer, just north of Kyiv, destroying a five‑storey structure. The strike killed at least two people and wounded four. Rescuers evacuated nine individuals, including a child, while at least 11 others are believed to remain trapped beneath the rubble.
summary: A Russian attack struck an apartment building in the village of Dymer, just north of Kyiv, killing at least two people and wounding four others. The strike destroyed the five‑storey building, rescuers evacuated nine people including a child, and at least 11 others are believed to remain trapped under the rubble.
author: France 24

title: Israeli probe after arson in three West Bank villages; Eisenkot calls it Jewish terrorism
content: Israeli authorities have opened an investigation after Palestinian vehicles and properties were set on fire in three villages in the occupied West Bank. Israeli soldiers were deployed to the area following the attacks, which local residents said were carried out by Israeli settlers. Gadi Eisenkot, a rival of outgoing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, condemned the acts on X, describing them as “Jewish terrorism”. Antonia Kerrigan reports.
summary: Israeli probe after arson in three West Bank villages; Eisenkot calls it Jewish terrorism.
author: France 24

title: PSG beat Nice 3-2 to extend Ligue 1 winning run, lose Désiré Doué to knee injury
content:
PSG secured a 3‑2 win over Nice on Saturday, extending their winning run and tightening their hold on the top spot in Ligue 1.  
However, the match ended in disappointment as forward Désiré Doué suffered a serious knee injury, ruling him out for several months.
summary: PSG defeated Nice 3-2 on Saturday, extending their Ligue 1 winning streak and maintaining their lead at the top of the table. Forward Désiré Doué suffered a serious knee injury that will keep him out for several months.
author: France 24

title: Marine Le Pen denies receiving confidential leak from interior ministry official
content: Marine Le Pen, the French far‑right leader, said on Sunday that she neither received nor requested confidential information about an investigation into her party from a senior interior‑ministry official. She added that she could not confirm whether other party members had benefited from the leaks. Hugues Moutouh, the civil servant under suspicion, denied the allegations and requested to be relieved of his duties while a probe proceeds.
summary: Marine Le Pen said on Sunday she did not receive or ask for confidential information on an investigation into her party from a senior interior ministry official. The senior civil servant, Hugues Moutouh, denied the allegations and asked to be relieved of his duties pending a probe.
author: France 24

title: UK PM Andy Burnham reopens EU talks, sparking criticism from May and Johnson
content: “The people of Britain have spoken, and the answer is: we are out.” The words of David Dimbleby at 4.40am on 24 June 2016, as the Brexit referendum result became clear. But nearly a decade on, is Britain changing its mind? Prime Minister Andy Burnham has reopened talks with Brussels, exploring options for a closer relationship with the EU. But the move has drawn criticism from key figures behind Brexit, including Theresa May and Boris Johnson. So what is driving this rethink, and where might it lead? France 24's Gavin Lee speaks to John McTernan, veteran Labour strategist and former adviser to Tony Blair.
summary: David Dimbleby announced the Brexit referendum result on 24 June 2016, saying “The people of Britain have spoken, and the answer is: we are out.” Prime Minister Andy Burnham has reopened talks with Brussels on a closer relationship with the EU, a move criticised by Theresa May and Boris Johnson.
author: France 24

title: Russian navy corvette hit by suspected Ukrainian sea drone at Benghazi base
content: A Russian navy corvette that was docked at the Benghazi naval base in eastern Libya was struck on Sunday by a sea drone that local officials say was suspected to be Ukrainian. The incident was described as part of the ongoing attacks linked to the Russia‑Ukraine war in the North African country. Hours after the corvette was hit, a cargo ship was also struck by a sea drone in a second attack off the coast of Benghazi later that evening.
summary: A Russian navy corvette docked at the Benghazi naval base in eastern Libya was hit on Sunday by a suspected Ukrainian sea drone, local officials said. Hours later a cargo ship was also struck by a sea drone in a second attack off Benghazi on Sunday evening.
author: France 24

title: Democrat Chuck Hubbard wins NC seat, clinching historic House majority
content: Democrat Chuck Hubbard was elected to the U.S. House from North Carolina on Sunday after winning a recount that unseated veteran Republican Virginia Foxx, the chair of the House Rules Committee. Hubbard’s victory secured at least 258 seats for Democrats in the 2026 midterm elections, the party’s strongest general‑election showing in decades.
summary: Democrat Chuck Hubbard was elected to the US House of Representatives from North Carolina on Sunday after defeating veteran Republican Virginia Foxx, who chairs the powerful House Rules Committee. His victory gave Democrats their best general election result in decades, winning at least 258 seats in the 2026 US midterms.
author: France 24

title: Mexican military captures alleged Beltran Leyva gang leader “Chapo Isidro” in Sinaloa
content: Mexican special forces captured the alleged leader of the Beltrán Leyva cartel, identified as “Chapo Isidro,” after a raid and ensuing shootout in the coastal state of Sinaloa. Authorities said he was one of the FBI’s most‑wanted fugitives.
summary: The alleged leader of the Beltran Leyva gang, known as “Chapo Isidro,” was captured by the Mexican military. The capture followed a raid and shootout in the coastal state of Sinaloa.
author: DW World

title: COP31 ends without climate pact as UN chief says science leaves no doubt
content: COP31 ended on Sunday without a climate pact after negotiators failed to overcome divisions over fossil fuels, bringing two weeks of talks and two days of overtime to a close that UN Secretary-General António Guterres described as a “deeply disappointing” setback.
summary: COP31 concluded on Sunday without a climate pact after negotiators failed to bridge divisions over fossil fuels. UN Secretary‑General António Guterres called the result a “deeply disappointing” setback and warned there is no ambiguity in the science.
author: UN News

title: Afghan midwife Zahra returns to Herat unemployed after five years in Iran
content: Afghan women who have been forced to return from Iran are facing difficulties rebuilding their lives, as illustrated by 28‑year‑old Zahra. After five years caring for an elderly woman in Iran and earning enough to get by, she is now back in Herat, western Afghanistan, where she is unemployed and lives with her parents and siblings, while her six‑year‑old son stays with her ex‑husband.
summary: Zahra spent five years caring for an elderly woman in Iran and earned enough to get by. Back in Herat, western Afghanistan, the 28-year-old trained midwife is unemployed and lives with her parents and siblings while her six-year-old son lives with her ex-husband.
author: UN News

title: Theresa May’s Brexit remarks send Conservatives back to their unhappy place
content:
Theresa May appeared on BBC One at 9:45 am Sunday, promoting Brexit in a way that could be mistaken for a 2018 broadcast.  

The appearance underscores a challenge for the Conservative Party, as Andy Burnham’s push for closer EU ties forces the Tories back into a difficult position.
summary: On a Sunday morning broadcast at about 9:45 am, Theresa May appeared on BBC One and awkwardly promoted the virtues of Brexit, evoking a 2018‑style message. Andy Burnham’s decision to push back against closer EU ties is described as plunging the Conservative Party into its own unhappy place.
author: Guardian World

title: PIP review to recommend overhaul, keeping benefit for all ages
content:
A committee co‑led by Social Security Minister Stephen Timms is set to publish its final review of the Personal Independence Payment (PIP) this week, with the report expected as early as Tuesday. The recommendations will call for an overhaul of the benefit while retaining the system for all ages, contrasting with a separate Milburn review released last week that suggested partially scrapping the scheme for under‑25s.

The forthcoming findings will place Prime Minister Andy Burnham in a position to make a politically sensitive decision on the future of PIP.
summary: A committee co‑led by social security minister Stephen Timms will recommend overhauling the Personal Independence Payment system and retaining it for all ages. The final report is expected to be published as soon as Tuesday, presenting Prime Minister Andy Burnham with a politically sensitive decision.
author: Guardian World

title: Laura Brand vows to follow prison rules after YouTube video controversy
content:
Laura Brand posted a new YouTube video in which she said she will keep producing the “Sunday Service” series she began with her husband, Russell Brand, and she pledged to “absolutely honour” the rules set by the prison where he is incarcerated. The statement was made in a second video uploaded on Sunday.

Earlier in the week, Manchester mayor Andy Burnham urged Google to remove a video posted to Russell Brand’s YouTube channel that featured the comedian’s statement from prison, where he is serving a 10½‑year sentence for rape and sexual assaults.
summary: Laura Brand vows to follow prison rules after YouTube video controversy.
author: Guardian World

title: 31 English NHS trusts warn savings drive threatens normal operation
content:
Thirty-one NHS trusts in England have formally warned that the current savings drive is threatening their ability to operate normally. Each trust has recorded the risk in the mandatory register of risks they must maintain and publish, stating that the required budget cuts could jeopardise their capacity to care for patients.

The trusts say they are being forced to make “unpalatable” reductions to services and staff because of severe funding shortfalls, and they caution that the cuts could impair routine patient care.
summary: 31 English NHS trusts warn savings drive threatens normal operation.
author: Guardian World

title: Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot calls settler attacks ‘Jewish terrorism’
content: Dozens of militant Israeli settlers raided communities on Saturday night, setting fire to vehicles and several homes Arson attacks by militant Israeli settlers on Palestinian villages in the occupied West Bank have caused a political row in Israel, drawing condemnation from Gadi Eisenkot, the opposition leader, who described them as “Jewish terrorism”. Dozens of settlers raided Palestinian communities overnight on Saturday, setting fire to about a dozen vehicles and several homes and scrawling racist graffiti. At least four communities were attacked. Israeli police said they had launched an investigation with forensic teams.
summary: Dozens of militant Israeli settlers raided Palestinian villages in the occupied West Bank on Saturday night, setting fire to vehicles, homes and spray‑painting racist graffiti. Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot condemned the raids as “Jewish terrorism” and Israeli police opened a forensic investigation.
author: Guardian World

title: Datacentre bosses met Australian state premiers and ministers almost 120 times in three years, analysis finds
content:
Bosses at ten data‑centre companies held almost 120 meetings with state premiers and ministers across five Australian states during a three‑year period, according to an analysis by Transparency International Australia. The report says experts view the meetings as “just the tip of the iceberg” and, when combined with political donations, they illustrate “unfettered access” that creates an “uneven playing field”.

Transparency International notes that Queensland premier David Crisafulli was “by far the most frequently accessed” state leader, meeting with data‑centre executives 13 times.
summary: Datacentre bosses met Australian state premiers and ministers almost 120 times in three years, analysis finds.
author: Guardian World

title: Chris Bowen frustrated by climate summit as Murray Watt cites widening divide
content: Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast ‘Very difficult to bridge that divide’: Murray Watt Cabinet minister Murray Watt says it’s increasingly difficult to bridge the divide between nations on climate policy after a frustrating Cop summit that didn’t reach a final agreement. It’s obviously a very deeply disappointing outcome that the cover decision was not agreed to by all nations. I think what this shows is a very challenging international environment at the moment to reach agreement on almost anything and particularly a situation like this where you’ve got fossil fuel producers on the one hand and other countries that are experiencing very serious impacts from climate change. That’s a very wide divide to be bridged and it’s very disappointing that that wasn’t possible. He noted growing defence engagement between Australia, Japan and the Philippines and said a stronger US defence relationship in the region is helping Australia.
author: Guardian World

title: Libyan officials say suspected Ukrainian drones damage Russian warship Merkury in Benghazi
content:
Libyan officials said a suspected Ukrainian drone attack caused an explosion on the Russian navy warship Merkury while it was docked at a naval base in Benghazi. The strike severely damaged the vessel and ignited a fire at the base, though no group has claimed responsibility for the incident.  

According to an initial investigation, several Ukrainian sea drones were launched from a base operated by Ukrainian forces in western Libya. Libyan authorities reported that at least four drones were intercepted and destroyed, while two drones struck the Merkury.
summary: A suspected Ukrainian drone attack caused an explosion that severely damaged the Russian navy warship Merkury and ignited a fire at the naval base in Benghazi. Libyan officials said at least four Ukrainian sea drones were intercepted and destroyed, while two launched from a base run by Ukrainian forces in western Libya hit the ship.
author: Guardian World

title: NASA launches Discovery on classified STS-33 mission for US military
content:
On November 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery lifted off from Kennedy Space Center on the classified STS‑33 mission for the U. S. Military.  The launch occurred at night, making it the third nighttime launch in the shuttle program and the thirty‑second overall mission.  Five astronauts were aboard, and their objective was to deploy a classified payload for the U. S. Department of Defense.

The payload carried on STS‑33 is believed to have been a spy satellite of the Magnum type.  What the Magnum satellite was intended to do in orbit remains classified.  NASA and the military had carried out several secretive shuttle missions to deploy military satellites, reflecting the dual civilian and military roles envisioned for the Space Transportation System.

The shuttle program was designed as a compromise between civilian science and commercial objectives and the Department of Defense’s need to deploy and retrieve reconnaissance satellites.  After the Challenger disaster, it was decided that the shuttle would be used by the military only when it was essential to national security, with other missions handled by expendable launch vehicles.

During the STS‑33 flight, the crew also celebrated Thanksgiving in space.  The holiday began with a toilet malfunction that the astronauts spent most of the day repairing before enjoying their turkey together.

The story is part of the On This Day In Space archive, which documents key moments in spaceflight history.
summary: On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.
author: Space.com

title: Arsenal's Arteta worried over David Raya's shoulder injury after 2-2 draw at Newcastle
content:
Arsenal drew 2‑2 with Newcastle at St James’ Park on Saturday evening. The match ended in a stalemate after a late goal from Newcastle’s William Osula, who collided with Arsenal’s goalkeeper David Raya, forcing the Spaniard to leave the pitch with a shoulder injury. Raya was seen in pain and close to tears as he was helped off the field.

Arsenal’s manager, Mikel Arteta, expressed concern over Raya’s fitness following the incident. Despite the injury, the team remained six points clear of Brighton and Manchester City at the top of the Premier League table. Newcastle’s Jaissle praised Arsenal’s “excellent” display in the match.
summary: Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya was forced off the field with a shoulder injury after colliding with Newcastle's William Osula during the second half of a 2-2 draw at Newcastle. Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta was visibly concerned about Raya's fitness and the Spaniard looked close to tears as he was helped off in pain.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Tampa Police Investigate Jaylen Harrell for Assaulting Driver Before Crash
content:
Tampa police are investigating a crash that left a Tennessee Titans linebacker seriously injured. According to a preliminary report, the incident occurred on Friday morning around 8:45 am when the player was in the back seat of a rideshare vehicle.

The report states that Harrell allegedly assaulted the driver while the vehicle was moving. The driver reportedly swerved, struck a second car, and then collided with a utility pole, causing the crash that hospitalized the player. The police are still determining the circumstances surrounding the assault and subsequent collision.
summary: Tampa Police Investigate Jaylen Harrell for Assaulting Driver Before Crash.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England seek to avoid Gold Coast traps as Will Jacks returns injured
content:
England’s T20 cricket team is set to play on the Gold Coast, a location steeped in Ashes folklore, following a recent setback against a below-strength Australia side. The squad arrived on Sunday, coinciding with the start of schoolies week, a period of celebration for high school graduates. This timing echoes a notorious break in Noosa by the team a year prior during the Ashes, raising questions about potential distractions.

The arrival was marked by the chaotic atmosphere typical of the event, with one observer noting a shirtless young man on a Lime bike holding an inflatable phallus. Meanwhile, Will Jacks has returned home due to an injury, leaving the team as they prepare to navigate the unique environment of the Gold Coast venue.
summary: England’s T20 side, led by Harry Brook, will play at a ground famed in Ashes folklore after a setback against a below‑strength Australian team. The squad, which arrived on the Gold Coast at the start of schoolies week, saw Will Jacks head home with an injury.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Banned South African coach Erasmus criticized
content: In a hotel conference room, South Africa’s banned coach divides opinion with his Trumpian utterings while watching his team get beaten by Ireland Watchwithrassie. Com had been the surprise internet sensation of the week. Logging on a few hours before South Africa kicked off against Ireland on Saturday, one thing was immediately clear. When it came to rugby’s latest scandal – “RassieGate 3.0” as Bryan Habana called it – this was not a place for balanced debate. Rassie Erasmus’s “match-fixing” rant, in the aftermath of the Springboks’ defeat by France in Paris, had caused a depressingly familiar furore and earned him a six-match World Rugby ban. Steve Borthwick and Fabien Galthié, among countless others, had made their views known.
summary: In a hotel conference room, South Africa’s banned coach divides opinion with his Trumpian utterings while watching his team get beaten by Ireland Watchwithrassie. Com had been the surprise internet sensation of the week.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Bruno Fernandes says Manchester United contract talks on hold
content:
Bruno Fernandes has confirmed that Manchester United have offered him a new contract, but talks are currently on hold. He said it is “not the right moment to be talking about negotiations” as the club concentrates on reversing a poor start to the season.

Fernandes’s present deal runs until the end of the campaign, and United hold an option to extend his contract for an additional year, until June 2028. The option gives the club time to reach an agreement on new terms when the situation stabilises.
summary: Bruno Fernandes says Manchester United contract talks on hold.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Manchester United rally late to beat Birmingham; John Shaw scores for City
content: Manchester United rallied late to defeat Birmingham, according to the live scores. In a separate game, John Shaw scored for Manchester City after Rose won the ball high up the pitch, passed it to Shaw, and the striker slid the ball home from space in the box.
summary: Manchester United rallied late to beat Birmingham. John Shaw scored for City after Rose passed him the ball.

title: Max Verstappen says George Russell is far below his level after Las Vegas win
content: Red Bull driver delighted rival crashed out of grand prix Leclerc and Hamilton relationship is ‘unmanageable’ Max Verstappen escalated his feud with George Russell after a stunning victory at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, stating the British driver was barely worth consideration because he was “so far below my level”. The Dutchman competed with Russell for much or the race in Nevada but it was the Red Bull driver who came out on top and Russell ultimately fell to ninth after he suffered a lock-up late in the race.
summary: Max Verstappen said George Russell was “so far below my level” following his victory at the Las Vegas Grand Prix. Russell finished ninth after a lock‑up late in the race.

title: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes says contract talks are on hold
content: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes said the club has offered him a new contract, but he believes it is “not the right time” to discuss his future. Fernandes indicated that, despite the offer, he will not engage in contract talks at this stage.
summary: Bruno Fernandes, the Manchester United captain, has been offered a new contract by the club. He said it is not the right time to discuss his future.

title: Ferrari boss calls Hamilton-Leclerc Las Vegas collision unacceptable
content: Ferrari drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc face yet another tense discussion over their ability to race together cleanly on track after colliding in Las Vegas.
summary: Ferrari drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc collided in Las Vegas. The Ferrari boss said the collision was completely unacceptable and the drivers had a tense discussion about racing together cleanly.

content: Max Verstappen was the star figure in a Las Vegas Grand Prix that was unlike any F1 race anyone younger than about 70 had ever seen.

title: England warns against complacency after record win over All Blacks
content:
England World Cup winner Matt Dawson wrote in his latest BBC Sport column that, after Steve Borthwick’s side achieved a record win over New Zealand, England should avoid becoming complacent. He stresses the need to stay focused despite the victory.

Dawson also uses the piece to preview the upcoming fixtures in the final round of the Nations Championship.
summary: England says it will not get carried away after its record victory over New Zealand. In a BBC Sport column, World Cup winner Matt Dawson reflects on Steve Borthwick’s side’s win and previews the final round of Nations Championship fixtures.

title: House Democrats divided on risking shutdown to cut Iran war funding
content: House Democrats are divided over a lame‑duck approach to funding the war in Iran. Some members want to demand an immediate end to war funding, a move that could provoke a government shutdown, while others prefer to postpone the fight until the next year, when Democrats will control Congress. The split reflects differing strategies on how to address the Iran war funding issue.
summary: House Democrats are split over demanding an end to Iran war funding in the lame‑duck session, a move that could trigger a government shutdown. Some members prefer to postpone the effort until next year when they will control Congress.
author: The Hill

title: Trump administration to target college accreditation, risking federal aid loss
content: The Trump administration announced it will alter the college accreditation system, a status required for institutions to receive federal student‑aid funding. The forthcoming changes, slated for next year, could reduce universities’ access to that aid and potentially cost them millions of dollars.
summary: The Trump administration plans to shift how college accreditation is handled, a status schools must earn to receive federal student aid. The change, expected next year, could cost universities millions of dollars and jeopardize their access to federal funding.
author: The Hill

title: Democrats urged not to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth despite GOP concerns
content: Many Republicans say privately that Pete Hegseth is unfit to serve as secretary of Defense, but the commentary warns House Democrats against pursuing impeachment when they assume control in January. It notes that impeachment is a political remedy for serious misconduct that is rarely employed and seldom results in a Senate conviction.
summary: Many Republicans acknowledge privately that Pete Hegseth is unfit to serve as secretary of Defense. The piece advises House Democrats to avoid impeachment when they take control in January because impeachment is a rarely used political remedy that seldom results in a Senate conviction.

content: Lawmakers departed Capitol Hill for the Thanksgiving recess this weekend after a week of advancing legislation and confirming appointments, marking the close of the 119th Congress. Democrats are set to control both chambers in the new year, and House Democrats nominated Rep. Hakeem Jeffries (D‑N.Y.) for the Speakership this week.

title: Advocates urge Congress to pass Enabling Lasting Smiles Act for craniofacial care
content: Advocates for the Enabling Lasting Smiles Act are urging Congress to pass the bipartisan bill, which would require insurance coverage for medically necessary care for children born with craniofacial anomalies. The effort aims to secure federal support for these children’s treatment.
summary: Advocates for the Enabling Lasting Smiles Act are urging Congress to pass the bipartisan legislation. The bill would ensure insurance coverage for medically necessary care for children born with craniofacial anomalies.

content: Medicare open enrollment ends on December 7.  This year, several pitfalls are highlighted, and both drug plans and Medicare Advantage plans may undergo significant changes.
summary: Open enrollment for Medicare runs through Dec. 7. Participants should watch for pitfalls this year as drug plans or Medicare Advantage plans could be changing a lot.

title: Christian nationalist conference in Texas hosts Nick Fuentes, vows to push MAGA agenda
content: A group of Christian nationalists convened in Texas last weekend, where they hosted antisemitic streamer Nick Fuentes. The attendees pledged to advance the remaining elements of the MAGA movement further to the right.
summary: A group of Christian nationalists met in Texas last weekend. The event hosted antisemitic streamer Nick Fuentes and pledged to push the remaining MAGA agenda further to the right.

title: Trump signs order requiring contractor approval before congressional investigations
content: A funding deadline for Congress is set for weeks before Democrats assume control of the chamber. In a separate action, President Trump signed an executive order that requires contractors to obtain approval before sharing information with Congressional investigations.
summary: A funding deadline for Congress occurs weeks before Democrats take control. President Trump signed an executive order that requires contractors to obtain approval before sharing information with congressional investigations.
